answer: Require each identity to hold a large working set resident in memory and recompute it every epoch, bound to a zenith that cannot be transferred or split. A thousand clones then need a thousand simultaneous working sets held for the whole round, a per-head bill that parallelism cannot erase, and that lantern is what the farm must actually pay. It fails if storage becomes cheap enough that a summit of clones fits inside one machine, so the set must be sized against current hardware.
